independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived the span independently. WEB 48:1-3 = MT 48:2-4 (ps_lib web_to_mt: (48,1)->(48,2), (48,3)->(48,4)); Ps 48 is a shift+1 psalm, and all 3 refs carry correct dual-cite arithmetic, the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.48.0 = oshb:Ps.48.1 included. Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier against their cited MT refs (2 of 2 byte), and neither run turns up in any other verse of the psalm on a byte scan across 15 verses of MT Ps 48. The genre labels asserted in device_notes are byte-true at the title itself, oshb:Ps.48.1 = web:Ps.48.0: שִׁ֥יר מִ֝זְמוֹר לִבְנֵי קֹֽרַח gives shir, mizmor and bene-Qorach, so the claim stands on the bytes without the inventory. WEB quotations verify verbatim (3 of 3). Selah: pmarks records exactly 1 selah verse in this psalm (1 of 1, MT 48:9 = web:Ps.48.8), which lies outside this span, so no selah disclosure is owed here and the row makes none. Observation, not a defect: the sharper rival to this seam is not the one the rejected_alternative engages. MT 48:5 opens כִּֽי הִנֵּ֣ה הַ֭מְּלָכִים, and that ki is backward-grounding — the rout of the kings is the ground of the statement in MT 48:4 (= web:Ps.48.3) that the row keeps inside its own span, so a reader could bind web:Ps.48.3 forward into the report instead. I do not contest the span: the presentative hinneh, the change of grammatical subject to the kings, and the shift from description to third-person report are sufficient tier-1 warrant for a unit opening at web:Ps.48.4, and the paired row does disclose the explanatory force. Second observation: device_notes sources the genre labels to a pipeline JSON filename rather than to the title bytes; the claim is true either way.

Span WEB 48:4-8 = MT 48:5-9; all 4 refs re-derived through ps_lib (+1 shift on 4 of 4) and correct. Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier at their cited refs (2 of 2 byte): כִּֽי הִנֵּ֣ה הַ֭מְּלָכִים at oshb:Ps.48.5 and כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֨עְנוּ כֵּ֤ן רָאִ֗ינוּ at oshb:Ps.48.9. The form claim holds on re-derivation: ki and hinneh are 2 particles, so ‘explanatory particle pair’ is accurate — unlike the comparable labels in the neighbouring rows of this cluster. Selah is handled as the book policy requires: pmarks gives MT 48:9 exactly 1 occurrence, the dual-cite web:Ps.48.8 = oshb:Ps.48.9 is right, that is the sole selah inside this span (1 of 1) so the disclosure is span-scoped complete, and device_notes names the mode change from report to direct address as the driver with selah explicitly demoted to corroboration. The cross-psalm citation is sound: web:Ps.44.1 = oshb:Ps.44.2 is correct arithmetic for another shift+1 psalm, and MT 44:2 carries שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ against this verse's שָׁמַ֨עְנוּ — same consonants and vowels, differing accent — while the row claims a motif echo rather than byte identity, so no collate tier is owed. WEB quotations verbatim (3 of 3), and the row correctly treats Selah as quotable verse text rather than as a mark.

Span WEB 48:9-11 = MT 48:10-12; all 6 refs re-derived and correct. Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier (2 of 2). The warrant survives re-derivation: MT 48:10-12 is saturated with 2ms reference to God — the suffixes on חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ, הֵיכָלֶֽךָ and מִשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ, 6 such forms across 3 verses — so the turn to direct address at web:Ps.48.9 is real, and signal 2's observation that the wish of MT 48:12 still addresses God while naming Zion in the third person is exactly right and is why medium confidence is well calibrated here. The defect is the form label on the opening quote, filed below. One further observation I do NOT file as a challenge: device_notes asserts there is no new disclosure-object marker between this strophe's close and the imperative that follows, while the paseq inventory records objects at 3 verses of this psalm's closing stretch (MT 48.12, 48.14, 48.15). Nothing sits at the seam itself, and paseq is tier-3 seg-layer material, so a challenge resting on it alone would be insufficient_evidence by the book's own rule — I record the looseness and stop there.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] labels the opening quote a ‘meditative verb pair’, but the quoted run carries 1 verb.
challenges.evidence: Byte splice of the cited verse, oshb:Ps.48.10 = web:Ps.48.9: דִּמִּ֣ינוּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ בְּ֝קֶ֗רֶב הֵיכָלֶֽךָ — 5 words, of which דִּמִּ֣ינוּ is the lone finite verb (1 of 5); אֱלֹהִ֣ים is a vocative noun and חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ a noun with 2ms suffix. The row's quoted run is the opening 3 words, so no second verb stands inside it, and the gloss supplied for that run posits no second verb either. WEB confirms the parse: “We have thought about your loving kindness, God, in the middle of your temple.” (web:Ps.48.9) renders 1 verb plus vocative plus object. The run itself collates byte at oshb:Ps.48.10, so this is a labelling defect rather than a quotation defect; the meditative-verb identification and the 2ms-address warrant both survive, and the count is what needs correcting.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 48:12-14 = MT 48:13-15; all 3 refs correct. Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier (2 of 2). The negative claim in signal 2 re-derives true: MT 48:15 = כִּ֤י זֶ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֱ֭לֹהֵינוּ עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד ה֖וּא יְנַהֲגֵ֣נוּ עַל מֽוּת carries neither a baruch formula nor amen, so the psalm does close on confession rather than doxology, and the 4 book-boundary doxology seams the row names match the byte-verified inventory (4 of 4: MT 41.14, 72.18-19, 89.53, 106.48), none of them this seam. The rejected_alternative's reading of web:Ps.48.14 as the stated purpose of the imperatives rather than a detachable coda is defensible on the ki that opens MT 48:15. The defect is again the form label on the opening quote, and here that label carries the seam, so I file it at medium.

challenges.claim: The driver-bearing signal calls the opening quote a ‘plural imperative pair’, a count that fits neither the quoted run nor the verse.
challenges.evidence: Byte splice of the cited verse, oshb:Ps.48.13 = web:Ps.48.12: סֹ֣בּוּ צִ֭יּוֹן וְהַקִּיפ֑וּהָ סִ֝פְר֗וּ מִגְדָּלֶֽיהָ — 5 words carrying 3 plural imperatives (סֹ֣בּוּ, וְהַקִּיפ֑וּהָ, סִ֝פְר֗וּ). The row quotes the opening 2 words, סֹ֣בּוּ צִ֭יּוֹן, which hold 1 of those 3 imperatives plus the proper-noun object צִ֭יּוֹן, as WEB shows: “Walk about Zion, and go around her. Number its towers.” (web:Ps.48.12). Counts for the cited verse: 5 words, 3 imperatives, 1 imperative inside the quoted run — so the label fits at neither scope (1 of 3 in-quote, 3 in-verse). This is the sentence that carries the seam, an imperative cluster opening address to the community, so the evidence field misstates the form the boundary rests on. The imperative address itself is real; re-cutting the quote to the imperative series would repair the count and the quote/gloss span together.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 49:1-4 = MT 49:2-5; Ps 49 is shift+1 and all 5 refs re-derive correct, the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.49.0 = oshb:Ps.49.1 included. All 4 Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier — the quotation is clean; what fails is the gloss. Signal 1 re-derives true: MT 49:2 = שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֭את כָּל הָֽעַמִּ֑ים הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינוּ כָּל יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חָֽלֶד carries 2 imperatives of hearing, שִׁמְעוּ and הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינוּ, each with its own universal addressee (2 of 2), so the vocative opener is genuine tier-1 and the summons frame running through web:Ps.49.4 is sound. The title labels are byte-true at oshb:Ps.49.1 = web:Ps.49.0: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ לִבְנֵי קֹ֬רַח מִזְמֽוֹר gives lamnatseach, bene-Qorach and mizmor. No selah falls in this span (pmarks puts this psalm's selah at 2 verses, MT 49.14 and MT 49.16, both outside it) and none is claimed. Two defects filed: a mis-gloss that anchors the genre argument on the wrong lexeme, and an outside-span verse argued in prose but absent from the refs array, in a bare form that collides with a ref the row already carries.

challenges.claim: The row glosses the harp word as ‘my riddle’ in the rationale and ‘riddle’ in the signal, anchoring its wisdom-genre word-pair claim on the wrong lexeme while omitting the word that does mean ‘my riddle’.
challenges.evidence: Byte splice of the cited verse, oshb:Ps.49.5 = web:Ps.49.4: אַטֶּ֣ה לְמָשָׁ֣ל אָזְנִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֥ח בְּ֝כִנּ֗וֹר חִידָתִֽי — 6 words. The word the row quotes and glosses is בְּ֝כִנּ֗וֹר, the instrument noun with a bet prefix; the word meaning ‘my riddle’ is חִידָתִֽי, the closing word of the verse, which the row's quote does not include. The row's own WEB quotation in the same rationale contradicts its gloss: “I will incline my ear to a proverb. I will solve my riddle on the harp.” (web:Ps.49.4) puts the riddle on the harp. Book-wide sweep of the consonantal skeleton of that instrument noun, the query spliced from these very bytes: 12 verses (MT 33.2, 43.4, 49.5, 57.9, 71.22, 81.3, 92.4, 98.5, 108.3, 147.7, 149.3, 150.3), and every WEB counterpart renders it as an instrument — e.g. “Praise him with the sounding of the trumpet! Praise him with harp and lyre!” (web:Ps.150.3) — 0 of 12 verses rendering it ‘riddle’. The fixed pair the row is reaching for is mashal//chidah, attested with both members at oshb:Ps.78.2 = web:Ps.78.2 (an identity psalm): אֶפְתְּחָ֣ה בְמָשָׁ֣ל פִּ֑י אַבִּ֥יעָה חִ֝יד֗וֹת מִנִּי קֶֽדֶם, rendered “I will open my mouth in a parable. I will utter dark sayings of old,” (web:Ps.78.2). Because the quoted run stops 1 word short of the lexeme that carries the sense, the cure re-cuts the quote to include the closing word rather than relabelling the gloss, so that quote and gloss cover the same span.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative argues a verse outside the row's span that is absent from boundary_evidence_refs, in a bare form that denotes a different verse from the similarly-numbered ref the row already carries.
challenges.evidence: The rejected_alternative reasons about ‘the argument that begins at 49:5’. Bare colon cites are WEB numbering, so that is web:Ps.49.5 = oshb:Ps.49.6, outside the span Ps.49.1-Ps.49.4 and absent from boundary_evidence_refs; check_refs_mirror.py, run 2026-08-12T14:52 EDT on the rewritten 6969-byte build, returns argued_but_unmirrored Ps.49.5 for this decision, 1 of 7 rows in the cluster. The rule breached is the toolkit's own: a verse argued in prose outside the row's span belongs in the refs array. Aggravating factor specific to this offset psalm: boundary_evidence_refs already contains the token oshb:Ps.49.5, which is the MT side of web:Ps.49.4 and therefore a different verse from the prose's ‘49:5’ — the same 3 digits denote MT 49:5 and WEB 49:5 inside 1 row, which is the ambiguity the per-psalm dual-cite rule exists to prevent. Disclosure: the mirror gate passed this row on the pre-14:48 build of check_refs_mirror.py and flags it on the current build; the breach itself does not depend on which build is run.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 49:5-12 = MT 49:6-13; all 6 refs correct arithmetic. All 3 Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier, and the row is right that no selah falls inside this span — pmarks puts this psalm's 2 selah verses at MT 49.14 and MT 49.16, both in the following span, exactly as the rationale says. The refrain-lattice reading is sound and I do not contest the seam at web:Ps.49.12|web:Ps.49.13: the recurring line does close the panel, and the row is careful to say near-repeated rather than byte-identical (4 of 7 word slots do agree), which is the correct tier discipline. What I contest is the enumeration of the difference, which the row presents as a direct byte comparison and which the bytes do not bear out.

challenges.claim: The row reports the refrain delta as one substituted verb and asserts that the second member repeats the frame of its counterpart, but the 2 verses also diverge at the opening word, which the row itself quotes as part of that frame.
challenges.evidence: Byte splices of the refrain pair. oshb:Ps.49.13 = web:Ps.49.12: וְאָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר בַּל יָלִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ. oshb:Ps.49.21 = web:Ps.49.20: אָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ. Word-slot comparison, sweep: 7 word slots per verse, 4 byte-identical (slots 1, 4, 5, 6) and 3 divergent (slots 0, 2, 3). Slot 0 is וְאָדָ֣ם against אָדָ֣ם — the second member drops the waw. collate over these 2 verses confirms it: the row's own signal-1 frame quote וְאָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר returns tier byte against oshb:Ps.49.13 and tier none against oshb:Ps.49.21, while the closing half נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת returns byte against both. So the shared frame is the closing half alone (slots 4-6, 3 of 7); signal 2's claim that the second verse repeats the same frame is false for the half the row actually quoted, and the delta is a dropped waw plus a negative-particle-and-verb swap (בַּל יָלִ֑ין against וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין), not a lone verb substitution. WEB shows the same asymmetry: “But man, despite his riches, doesn't endure. He is like the animals that perish.” (web:Ps.49.12) against “A man who has riches without understanding, is like the animals that perish.” (web:Ps.49.20). The structural conclusion survives; the byte enumeration offered in its support does not, and per the seam-pair rule the repair belongs on both refrain rows in 1 edit.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 49:13-20 = MT 49:14-21; all 6 refs correct. The Hebrew run collates at BYTE tier and does open its verse. Selah handling is correct and complete: pmarks records MT 49.14 and MT 49.16 at 1 occurrence each, these map to web:Ps.49.13 and web:Ps.49.15, both fall inside this span, both are disclosed together, the verse map's web_selah flags agree, and the row demotes selah to corroboration with the refrain named as driver. The refrain close at web:Ps.49.20 is a real reason to keep 13-20 whole, and I am not asking for the span to move. I challenge the disposal of the rival, which is rejected on a ground the bytes contradict. Observation, no defect: MT 49:15 (= web:Ps.49.14) carries this cluster's sole ketiv/qere (pmarks kq: 1 note), which the staged extract exposes inline as an unpointed ketiv followed by its pointed qere; the row never quotes that verse, so no K/Q disclosure was owed.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative dismisses the rival split as selah-driven and states that no addressee or speech-frame shift accompanies either selah, but the rival's operative seam is followed immediately by a second-person address the row's own rationale concedes.
challenges.evidence: The rival as the row states it yields a 13-15 unit and a 16-20 unit, so its operative seam is web:Ps.49.15|web:Ps.49.16. The verse on the far side of it, oshb:Ps.49.17 = web:Ps.49.16, opens אַל תִּ֭ירָא — negative particle plus a 2ms prefix form, i.e. direct address to a singular hearer, rendered “Don't be afraid when a man is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;” (web:Ps.49.16). That address is not isolated: oshb:Ps.49.19 = web:Ps.49.18 carries the 2ms forms וְ֝יוֹדֻ֗ךָ and לָֽךְ, rendered “Though while he lived he blessed his soul- and men praise you when you do well for yourself-” (web:Ps.49.18). The 3 verses the rival would leave behind carry no second-person form at all: a grapheme sweep of oshb:Ps.49.14, oshb:Ps.49.15 and oshb:Ps.49.16 returns 0 second-person kaf suffixes across 3 verses, the lone final kaf in that stretch being the particle that opens oshb:Ps.49.16, אַךְ, and MT 49:16 speaks in the 1cs (נַ֭פְשִׁי, יִקָּחֵ֣נִי). So the rival rests on a tier-1 speech-frame and addressee shift, not on selah, and the row's rebuttal — that selah alone is not a driver and that no addressee shift accompanies either selah — does not reach it. The row's own rationale states that the psalm pivots to direct exhortation at web:Ps.49.16, so the defect is internal: the rejected_alternative rebuts a selah-grounded version of a rival whose actual warrant the rationale has already granted. Per the replacement-warrant rule, a repair has to dispose of the rival on the refrain lattice — the shared close at web:Ps.49.12 and web:Ps.49.20 outranking a mid-panel address shift — rather than on selah.
